teaser: Each reference's licence, access, links and quotes, reading a paywalled article through its shadow, and paying the sources we use.
core_idea: Every reference carries primitives worth recording (licence, access, links, quotes, quality, history); when an article cannot be read, the shadow of who cites and quotes it is evidence, as Wikipedia's paywalled citations show, and disagreements between shadow and source become visible, building a record of who got it right and a basis for paying the sources used.

not to read around the wall, but to pay through it, per use, for what we actually cite.

figures.caption: Seeing an article through its shadow: a paywalled article we hold no licence for, at the centre, and around it what we can read: Wikipedia, whose editors read it, cite it and quote it; other outlets that quote, summarise or disagree with it; social posts that pull out one line; and our own captures, which keep every quote with its source.

What every reference should carry, recorded each time a page is captured: its licence; its access; its links, out and in; its quotes, made and received; its quality; its history; and who to pay. Proposed; the access and the history are already recorded by the PHP site's source watch.

The PHP site's source watch: a vault that watches every outside source on the story, 913 pages from 597 publishers in 59 countries, in 34 languages, recording what access it had on each run and keeping a new snapshot whenever the content changed, 2,946 snapshots and graphs over 38 runs.

Every reference in Wikipedia's PHP2Shell article, as the PHP site reads it: 43 references at revision 1381798757, 16 of them pages the site's evidence vault holds, the others not yet captured, including The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal; for each, its publisher, which of the article's statements cite it, and which of the site's own claims rest on it.
